Note regarding the `new-api-needs-documentation` label:

This serves as a reminder for when your PR is modifying a ref *.cs file and adding/modifying public APIs, to please make sure the API implementation in the src *.cs file is documented with triple slash comments, so the PR reviewers can sign off that change.

issue_context.title: Add Thread.UnsafeStart to avoid capturing the ExecutionContext
comments: Maybe `void UnsafeStart(object? parameter = null)`? What's the policy on using default parameter values in the BCL?

review_comments: I assume we can't name this ([as we do regular thread pool threads](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/ThreadPool.cs#L1063)) as folks could have taken advantage of the fact that we start a new nameless thread and be doing the naming themselves?
It would technically be a breaking change to add a name to a thread that didn't previously have one and on which user code runs.  Whether it would actually break apps in practice, I don't know.
Yeah, I don't think it's worth it. It wasn't named in .NET Framework either.

Can we name it too while you're here? 
BTW, why does Linux FSW use Task.Factory.Start(..LongRunning..) but OSX starts a thread?

> Can we name it too while you're here?

There are other threads started by the libraries besides these.  I'd rather someone do an audit specifically for naming and ensure names are consistent, rather than doing a one-off here.  I only touched this one because it could safely use UnsafeStart because ExecutionContext is flowed differently.

> BTW, why does Linux FSW use Task.Factory.Start(..LongRunning..) but OSX starts a thread?

They were implemented by two different people?
Fair enough.
I suspect you will need a dummy implementation for Mono Browser.
Yup
Probably worth looking to see if there are other threads that need to do this. Like the FileSystemWatcher threads.

As part of this change I did an audit of all threads we're creating in dotnet/runtime; the ones I changed in this PR were the only ones that looked appropriate.  The FileSystemWatcher ones aren't appropriate as they raise user events; it's only fine for macOS (which I changed) as ExecutionContext is already flown manually there.
Then we're gonna need an overload to disable it over there as it captures the context. I'll fill another bug. Anything created lazily is notorious for capturing the wrong execution context
You already opened https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/30954 in September.
Ah yes
This might warn on mono browser build, that is why we had the if def, maybe suppress the warning?
Ah ok. It may be better to disable the warning instead of the ifdef to make it self-documenting.

The ifdef as it was written is broken.  It would mean that in the browser code that did:
```C#
Task.Factory.StartNew(() => DoStuff(), TaskCreationOptions.LongRunning);
```
would nop rather than eventually running DoStuff.

I will suppress the warning.  Thanks.
could also potentially check that culture didn't flow?
Why?
Just something else that wouldn't flow. But I guess this is fine.
It flows via AsyncLocals.
Ah I didn't know that.
Yeah, in .NET Core, ExecutionContext is entirely about AsyncLocal... for anything to flow, it's done via AsyncLocal.
